items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The visible SIMD helpers use cryptic names outside of loop counters: `m1`, `m2`, `ab`, `cc`, `mm`, `L`, `v`, and `K`/`k` in `y16(k: *const ChrK, K: V16i16)`. Some comments are present (e.g. "Store N pixels of r,g,b(,a) bytes"), and the kernel structure is fairly clear.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Kernels are split into main/kernels/simd with shared @Vector helpers. But src/main.zig is about 30.8KB (over 500 lines, which caps this item), the diff commits .zig-cache and the zig-out .so build artifacts, and the tools/*.py dev scripts with hist.py and hist2.py near-duplicates are left in place.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No visible validation of create-time inputs. The tools scripts swallow subprocess failures (`capture_output=True`, and a missing output is replaced with `b""`). The kernels use magic constants such as 255 and shift amounts. No resource leaks are visible, but validation at the boundaries cannot be confirmed.

items.name: Geometry, stride and tail handling
items.name_zh: 几何尺寸、步长与尾部处理
items.evidence: tools/sizes.py tested odd sizes (641x479, 33x17), 34x18, 1922x1082, other scale output sizes and all three algorithms, with 0 failures. Handling of strides larger than the row and NULL returns for unsupported combinations cannot be verified from the visible code.

items.name: ABI and build-target conformance
items.name_zh: ABI 与构建目标符合要求
items.evidence: `nm -D --defined-only` shows 3 exported symbols, and build.zig pins x86-64-v3 with no AVX-512 in the output. The library links only libc, contains no FFmpeg code and is single-threaded.
